name: Leo VI, the Wise (the Philosopher)
bio: J. M. Neale calls Leo VI the Philosopher a royal poet who reigned from 886 to 917 and left behind the Idiomela, or detached stanzas, on the Resurrection, sung at Lauds; they are better, he says, than might have been expected from an imperial author. His heading gives 917 as the year of death, while John Brownlie's heading for the hymn given here says he died in 911.
This file contains the one poem the sources attribute to him, Brownlie's 1900 translation of a hymn headed 'By the Emperor Leo VI.', which begins 'Come ye people, come adore Him'.

poems.title: Come ye people, come adore Him
poems.author: Leo VI, the Wise (the Philosopher)
poems.text:
Come ye people, come adore Him,
God in Holy Trinity;
God the Father, Son, and Spirit,
Ever Blessed Unity.

Thine the glory, God Almighty,
To the Son and Spirit given,
Ere upon the world's creation
Dawned the new-born light of heaven.

Holy, holy, we adore Thee,
One in power, in nature one;
God the Father, God the Spirit,
God the Co-Eternal Son.

By the Son the wide creation
Rose where chaos held its sway;
By the Spirit, God Almighty
Swept eternal night away.

Son, the Father's love revealing,
Son, through whom the Spirit came,
Blessed Godhead! endless glory
Be to Thine exalted name.
